scenes.title: 3:00 PM Study Lounge: 10-Minute Brass-Timer Crisp Wakeup vs 30-Minute Heavy Couch Fog
scenes.era: 2006 Flinders University & 2021 Paris Brain Institute afternoon nap protocol

layout.description: Sun-dappled mid-century leather study recliner beside a low walnut side table holding a mechanical brass kitchen timer and a heavy brass sphere poised above a porcelain saucer.

positions.who: 48-year-old architect / professional (stylized 2.5D vinyl character in rolled-sleeve oxford shirt reclining in leather armchair)
positions.where: reclined at 45 degrees with right hand loosely holding a heavy brass sphere over a floor saucer beside a 10-minute mechanical dial timer
positions.facing: three-quarter view toward the walnut side table

positions.who: Sleep physiologist (stylized 2.5D vinyl character in tailored charcoal cardigan and white coat holding a stopwatch)
positions.where: standing beside the study chair observing the exact moment finger tension relaxes at minute 10
positions.facing: angled toward the recliner and floor saucer

props.name: Polished brass sphere held loosely above a resonant white porcelain floor saucer
props.period_detail: Edison-style Paris Brain Institute N1 sleep-onset drop weight with zero electronic displays
props.physical_behavior: State A fingers cradle the gleaming brass sphere as shoulders soften into light rest -> State B fingers relax open and the brass sphere drops clattering sharply onto the saucer

props.name: Mechanical brushed-steel 10-minute vs 30-minute rotary dial timer
props.period_detail: tactile twist-dial bell timer sitting on walnut side table
props.physical_behavior: State A twisted crisply to the short 10-minute wedge -> State B rings a single bright bell as the sleeper sits straight up alert and energized

actions.verb_sequence: twists the mechanical dial to a brief 10-minute wedge and reclines holding the brass sphere -> drops the sphere onto the saucer at light sleep onset and sits upright instantly sharp

reactions.reaction: records immediate high-speed post-nap reaction without a trace of 30-minute delta grogginess

scenes.wardrobe: Crisp rolled-sleeve sky-blue oxford shirt and chinos; researcher in white coat over charcoal knit.
scenes.lighting: Warm afternoon window light filtered through wooden venetian blinds.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ten minutes of light sleep gives you two and a half hours of razor-sharp focus—while twenty extra minutes drops you off a deep-sleep cliff!

key_visual.description: an adult reclining in a study armchair whose relaxing fingers drop a gleaming brass sphere onto a porcelain saucer beside a 10-minute mechanical bell timer, snapping upright refreshed

positions.where: striding briskly along the sunlit outdoor courtyard path carrying a leather sketchbook

props.name: Open leather architectural sketchbook and fountain pen
props.period_detail: tactile cream paper pages flipping cleanly in outdoor breeze
props.physical_behavior: hand sketches rapid clean geometry lines immediately after rising from the 10-minute rest

actions.verb_sequence: steps out onto the sunlit courtyard path right after the 10-minute bell -> sketches rapid insight lines with crisp energy

reactions.reaction: alert upright stride holding steady through the whole late afternoon

scenes.wardrobe: Sky-blue oxford shirt with navy blazer slung over arm.

scenes.title: The 30-Minute Sofa Crash Contrast: Deep Delta Hangover

layout.description: Dimmed living-room sofa with heavy throw blanket where a 30-minute sleeper sits up rubbing forehead in sluggish confusion.

positions.where: slumped on the edge of a deep sofa tangled in a heavy throw blanket

props.name: Heavy wool throw blanket and 30-minute rotary timer
props.period_detail: thick woven blanket weighing over shoulders
props.physical_behavior: sleeper tugs sluggishly at the heavy blanket while struggling to stand upright

actions.verb_sequence: sleeps past minute 20 into deep slow waves -> wakes at minute 30 slumped and heavy-headed for 35 minutes

scenes.recognition_hook: Crossing thirty minutes plunges a tired brain into deep slow-wave delta sleep that takes half an hour to shake off.
